1. Purpose

This Agreement is entered into for the purpose of preventing unauthorised disclosure of Confidential Information exchanged between the parties in connection with IT services, hardware repair, data destruction, or related consulting engagements.

2. Definition of Confidential Information

2.1 "Confidential Information" means any data, documentation, or information disclosed by either party in any form (written, oral, visual, electronic, or otherwise), including but not limited to:

  • Business data stored on IT equipment
  • Personal data subject to UK GDPR
  • Technical specifications and system configurations
  • Client lists, financial information, and trade secrets
  • Source code, algorithms, and proprietary software
  • Network topologies, access credentials, and security configurations
  • Any information marked as "Confidential" or reasonably understood to be confidential

2.2 Oral Disclosures: Information disclosed orally shall be treated as Confidential Information if it is identified as confidential at the time of disclosure and summarised in writing within fourteen (14) days.

3. Obligations of the Receiving Party

The Receiving Party agrees to:

  1. Hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence
  2. Not disclose Confidential Information to third parties without prior written consent
  3. Use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose stated above
  4. Take reasonable measures to protect Confidential Information from unauthorised access
  5. Return or securely destroy all Confidential Information upon request or completion of services
  6. Limit access to Confidential Information to personnel with a genuine need to know
  7. Ensure that any authorised personnel are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those contained herein

4. Exclusions

This Agreement does not apply to information that:

  • Was publicly available at the time of disclosure
  • Becomes publicly available through no fault of the Receiving Party
  • Was lawfully in the Receiving Party's possession prior to disclosure
  • Was independently developed without use of Confidential Information
  • Is received from a third party lawfully entitled to disclose it
  • Is required to be disclosed by law, court order, or regulatory authority

5. Permitted Disclosures

Statutory Protection (Victims and Prisoners Act 2024 / Employment Rights Act 2025)

Nothing in this Agreement prevents either party from: making a protected disclosure (whistleblowing); reporting criminal conduct to law enforcement or regulators; seeking legal advice; or making disclosures relating to harassment or discrimination. Any such disclosure shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement.

6. Data Destruction Compliance

Certified Standards
  • NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1: Guidelines for Media Sanitization (Purge level minimum)
  • IEEE 2883-2022: Standard for Sanitizing Storage
  • NCSC Sanitisation Guidance: UK National Cyber Security Centre
  • HMG InfoSec Standard No. 5: UK Government sanitization requirements
  • ISO/IEC 21964 (DIN 66399): Physical destruction standards

Certificates of Destruction are provided for all data-bearing media processed. Destruction logs are retained for a minimum of six (6) years.

7. Data Processing (UK GDPR Article 28)

To the extent Jake Fieldhouse Consulting Ltd processes personal data on behalf of the Disclosing Party:

  • Processing shall occur only in accordance with documented instructions
  • All personnel with access are bound by confidentiality obligations
  • Appropriate technical and organisational measures are implemented (Article 32)
  • Sub-processors shall not be engaged without prior written consent
  • Personal data breach notification within 72 hours
  • Personal data deleted or returned upon completion of services

This clause satisfies Article 28 of UK GDPR. Practices will be reviewed in accordance with the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

9. Limitation of Liability

Liability Cap

Total aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of: (a) fees paid under the services agreement; or (b) £100,000. This limitation does not apply to death or personal injury, fraud, wilful misconduct, or any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

10. Intellectual Property & Trade Secrets

Each party retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property. Trade secrets disclosed under this Agreement are protected in accordance with the Trade Secrets (Enforcement, etc.) Regulations 2018 and common law principles of breach of confidence.

11. Term

This Agreement remains in effect for a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, or until terminated by mutual written agreement. Confidentiality obligations in respect of trade secrets shall survive indefinitely.

12. Force Majeure

Neither party shall be liable for failure or delay caused by events beyond reasonable control, including: acts of God, war, terrorism, pandemic, government actions, cyber-attacks, or critical infrastructure disruption. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than ninety (90) days, either party may terminate without liability.

13. Governing Law & Dispute Resolution

This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of England and Wales. Before initiating court proceedings, the parties agree to attempt resolution through good faith negotiation and, if unsuccessful, mediation through CEDR or a mutually agreed mediator.
